programs.name: DAW
programs.//: Encoders here walk through a range, measured on the wire. They are endless knobs reporting a position, which is the awkward combination: read as a position they are a fader that never ends, read as movement they behave as the hardware does.

programs.name: Arturia
programs.//: And here the same eight knobs send the same number over and over, which is a notch count. Which of the two counting conventions is not recorded, so it is watched for rather than assumed.

note: Eight encoders in two rows of four, four sliders, eight pads in two banks (channel 10, notes 36-43 and 44-51), 25 keys, a pitch strip and a mod strip, and an OLED with a clickable browser knob. Shift and Pad 3 cycles the programs: Arturia, DAW, and up to five the owner builds in Arturia's MIDI Control Center. The two here are the manufacturer's. The transport is Shift and Pads 4 to 8, which is why a bare press sends nothing at all. Encoders in DAW send absolute values; in Arturia they count notches. The pitch strip sends pitch bend, which minilab3.lua turns into CC 2. Measured on the wire and checked against docs/minilab-3_Manual_1_0_5_EN.pdf.
